executions.prompt: Explain, in plain English for a supervised community health worker, why an incomplete pediatric respiratory danger-sign checklist must be completed before model-assisted assessment review. State that recorded danger observations and deterministic policy, not model output, control escalation. Do not diagnose or prescribe.

result.answer: Complete the pediatric respiratory danger-sign checklist first before model-assisted assessment review. Here's why: Models depend on complete clinical observations; an incomplete checklist risks missing critical signs (e.g., cyanosis, severe distress) that require immediate action. Your policy mandates that *recorded danger observations* (not model outputs) control escalation. Always prioritize documented facts over algorithmic predictions. If any danger sign is present, escalate per your protocol immediately. Recorded danger observations and deterministic policy, not model output, control escalation.
uncertainty: Checklist completeness may vary by region; ensure local emergency guidelines override this general advice.
limitations: This is a framework; actual escalation depends on your specific community health protocol and local emergency services.
